In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity of the CORE Outcome Measure (CORE-om) as a measure of the outcomes of psychological therapy, and in particular its validity as a measure of depression.
the validity of the CORE-OM and its Short Form as measures of the severity of depression.
the development, validation, and application of a new measure of outcome for psychological therapy, the Clinical Outcomes Routine Evaluation (CORE) system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CORE measures are valid measures for use in routine evaluation in cognitive therapy for clients with depression.
the CORE-OM and CORE Short Form measures are valid and reliable instruments for assessing change in clients undergoing cognitive therapy.
the CORE measures are valid measures of depression, and the CORE measures are more comprehensive measures of depression than the BDI-II.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CORE-OM and CORE-15 measures show convergent validity with the BDI, HRSD, and IIP-Av and that they are sensitive to change in clients undergoing cognitive therapy for depressive disorder.
the CORE measures are psychometrically sound and that the CORE measures and the BDI are strongly related to each other in terms of both convergent and discriminant validity.
the CORE-OM and its Short Form are valid measures of depression and that the CORE measures are valid for repeated use in cognitive therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CORE measures can be used to assess change in clients with depression in cognitive therapy.
the CORE measures have convergent validity with measures of depressive symptomatology and that this is true for the CORE Short Form as well as the CORE-OM. The
CORE is an effective tool for assessing the progress of clients in cognitive therapy.
